about: Claims and who says them (Docs/Design/84 §7.7, Phase 1). A belief (struct Belief, Core/RatwRoads.h) carries a kind from this file, the one it is about (subject: #x.*#), a second party where there is one (object, the victim: #y.*#) and a place (a cell: #place.words#, World::placeWords). Each kind is said from up to five points of view: `they` (told of others), `victim` (the object telling it), `to_victim` (told to the object), `self` (the subject speaking of it) and `kin`. A point of view is a list of wordings, the first that can be filled is said; a claim with no wording that can be filled is never spoken. `family` is the old topic.claim_kind the lines answer in kind (facts.json); `topic` is the ambient topic it is talked of under (gossip unless it says); `topic_kind` sets topic.kind for that topic's lines; `grave` 0-3 is how heavy it is. `text` maps the free words older saves and the Watch still use onto a kind (`exact` or `starts`), tried in this file's order. #claim.charge# is the charge a warrant names; #claim.text# the free words themselves, the last resort for a kind about people.

self: I never laid a paw on #y.first#'s things
I never took a thing of #y.first#'s

they: #x.name# was robbed by someone nobody could make out
victim: I was robbed, and I never saw who did it
to_victim: you were robbed, and nobody saw who did it

they: #x.name# was set upon by someone nobody could make out
victim: I was set upon, and I never saw who did it
to_victim: you were set upon, and nobody saw who did it

they: #x.name# is wanted by the Watch for #claim.charge#
self: the Watch has my name up

they: there's a band of robbers camped #place.words#
